topic: Reperfusion times in acute myocardial infarction

audits.title: Patients presenting with acute myocardial infarction to a district general hospital: baseline results and effect of audit.
audits.standard: Cardiovascular Health Strategy: thrombolysis within ninety minutes of alerting medical or ambulance services
audits.setting: Letterkenny General Hospital, Donegal, district general hospital

cycle1.result: Thrombolysis given in 31%; median call to needle time 200 minutes (rural median 227.5 minutes, n = 64; urban median 175 minutes, n = 37). Median arrival to CCU 90 minutes.

audits.other_findings: Median time from symptom onset to calling for help was 119 minutes; 29% were more than 30 miles from the hospital.
audits.citation: O'Neill J, Dowling J, Wright P, Murphy AW, Bury G, Tedstone-Doherty D, et al.. Patients presenting with acute myocardial infarction to a district general hospital: baseline results and effect of audit. Ir Med J. 2003;96(3):70-73. PMID: 12722781.

audits.title: Increased prescription of thrombolytic treatment to elderly patients with suspected acute myocardial infarction associated with audit.
audits.standard: Prescription of thrombolytic treatment to elderly patients with acute myocardial infarction
audits.setting: Coronary care unit, Derriford Hospital, Plymouth (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: Thrombolysis prescribed to 13/110 (12%) patients aged 65 or over with confirmed myocardial infarction; no patients with angina received it.

audits.intervention: Interventions in clinical management (details not specified in abstract).

cycle2.result: Thrombolysis prescribed to 55/119 (46%) (p less than 0.01); 13/79 (16%) with angina treated.

audits.other_findings: Fewer exclusions for dyspepsia and unstated reasons; side effects more common in inferior than anterior infarcts (30% v 13%).
audits.citation: Hendra TJ, Marshall AJ. Increased prescription of thrombolytic treatment to elderly patients with suspected acute myocardial infarction associated with audit. BMJ. 1992;304(6824):423-425. doi:10.1136/bmj.304.6824.423. PMID: 1547391.

audits.title: Thrombolysis in acute myocardial infarction: an audit of practice.
audits.setting: Coronary care unit, Royal Hallamshire Hospital, Sheffield (teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: 212/335 (63%) received thrombolysis; withheld inappropriately in 8 cases and given inappropriately in 2; inpatient mortality 12% with vs 26% without thrombolysis (p < 0.005).

audits.other_findings: Streptokinase stopped in 5 (4%) for allergy or arrhythmia; guideline adjustment suggested.
audits.citation: Woodmansey PA, Caldicott LD, Channer KS. Thrombolysis in acute myocardial infarction: an audit of practice. J R Coll Physicians Lond. 1993;27(1):40-44. doi:10.1016/s0035-8819(25)01062-1. PMID: 8426340.

audits.title: Evaluation of the effectiveness of guidelines, audit and feedback: improving the use of intravenous thrombolysis in patients with suspected acute myocardial infarction.
audits.standard: Guideline-based use of intravenous thrombolysis in eligible patients with suspected acute MI
audits.setting: Five district general hospitals in North West Thames Region

cycle1.result: Eligible cases receiving thrombolysis: 94%, 60%, 58% and 57% in the four study hospitals; 53% in the control hospital (2593 patients overall).

audits.intervention: Guidelines with repeated audit and feedback (three further audits over a year).

cycle2.result: 88%, 92% (+32%), 95% (+37%) and 77% (+20%, printed as 7796); control rose to 68% (+15%); trend significant in the second and third hospitals only.

audits.other_findings: Appropriateness rose with treatment rates, but continued auditing at high rates may have reduced appropriateness.
audits.citation: Robinson MB, Thompson E, Black NA. Evaluation of the effectiveness of guidelines, audit and feedback: improving the use of intravenous thrombolysis in patients with suspected acute myocardial infarction. Int J Qual Health Care. 1996;8(3):211-222. doi:10.1093/intqhc/8.3.211. PMID: 8885185.

audits.title: Audit of prehospital thrombolysis by general practitioners in peripheral practices in Grampian.
audits.setting: General practices at least 30 minutes from Aberdeen Royal Infirmary, Grampian

cycle1.result: 146 (35%) of 414 thrombolytic administrations given by GPs and 268 (65%) deferred to hospital; standard readily achieved when GPs gave treatment, not otherwise.

audits.intervention: Periodic feedback of audit findings to GPs with practice case reviews.
audits.other_findings: Knowledge of benefits and feedback did not increase prehospital thrombolysis use.
audits.citation: Rawles J, Sinclair C, Jennings K, Ritchie L, Waugh N. Audit of prehospital thrombolysis by general practitioners in peripheral practices in Grampian. Heart. 1998;80(3):231-234. doi:10.1136/hrt.80.3.231. PMID: 9875080.
